steps.title: Carry it flat
steps.text: In the footwell or the boot, on a flat surface, with the air conditioning on. Never on a lap or a seat.

steps.title: Keep it cool
steps.text: A cool room out of the sun until it's served. Not the fridge: it dulls sugar flowers.

steps.title: Cut it from the edge
steps.text: Lift off the top tier first. Cut each tier in strips, then strips into fingers, with a long knife dipped in hot water.

steps.title: Eat it in two days
steps.text: Wrapped, at room temperature. Take out any wires and stems before serving.

care.keep: Keeping the top tier? Take off the flowers, wrap it twice in cling film and once in foil, and freeze it for up to three months.

questions.q: How far ahead should we book?
questions.a: For a wedding, six to twelve months; summer Saturdays go first. Three weeks for a birthday cake.

questions.q: Do we need the design when we book?
questions.a: No. Hold the date first; we draw the cake three months before.

questions.q: Can each tier be a different flavour?
questions.a: Yes, any of the season's flavours, one per tier.
Yes, iced to match. They cost about the same to decorate, so they rarely save much.

questions.q: Can our florist put fresh flowers on the cake?
questions.a: Yes. Send us their list first: many florists' flowers aren't safe near food, and we'll suggest swaps.

questions.q: Is it served as dessert or in the evening?
questions.a: Either. For the evening, most couples plan finger portions for about three quarters of their guests.

questions.q: Can you put a name or an age on it?
questions.a: Yes, piped or in sugar letters.
Yes, from the studio by appointment, in a box with carrying advice.

questions.q: Can you match our brand colours?
questions.a: Yes. Send us the colour codes and we'll match them in icing and show you a sample.
We plan three, with the cake. Four if there's no cake.

questions.q: Do you deliver and set up?
questions.a: Yes, across London and the Home Counties. We stack and finish the cake at the venue.

questions.q: Can you make a vegan cake, or one without wheat flour?
questions.a: Vanilla and berries can be made vegan, or with gluten-free flour. Our kitchen handles gluten, so it's not for coeliacs.
